attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. The Voss and Acher quotes nearby are separate from the claimed sentence.

semantics.note: Faithful. It keeps 'never', 'anything' and 'everything ... mimicry'. 'Worlds' is fairly read as 'world models'. The statement is a firm, unhedged universal about LLMs as of the post date.

contract.note: The plain reading of 'proper world model' (coherent, robust, usable, possibly implicit) is ordinary and not stretched either way. Limiting scope to general-purpose LLMs fits the context. The result still turns on what counts as robust, since Marcus set no threshold.

evidence.note: WM-ABench, available 2025-06-27, finds major world-modelling weaknesses in o3, GPT-4o and others. This backs a narrower concern but does not show that LLMs lack world models in every domain or that all their behaviour is mimicry.
Finds linear space and time representations in Llama-2. The authors explicitly do not show these form a causal world model used for inference, so this does not meet the contradiction condition.
Causal evidence of an entity-attribute binding mechanism in LLaMA and Pythia. It cuts against pure surface mimicry, but binding alone is not robust tracking and updating of world state.
GPT-3.5 tracks entities above a strong baseline, but becomes brittle on harder operations, and behavioural evidence alone does not settle the mechanism. Short of a robust, controlled world model.

reviews.rationale: Neither condition is met. No item shows a general-purpose LLM robustly building and using a coherent world model with controls against memorisation, so the claim is not contradicted. Selected failures (e1) cannot establish 'never' or 'everything', and e2–e4 show partial structured representations that weaken a pure-mimicry account. The packet does not settle the universal claim.
